answer:
**Dropout makes training less dependent on any one feature.** During training, randomly remove some activations so the model cannot always rely on exactly the same combination. During evaluation, use all features. This introduces noise into training; it is a regularization technique, not a method for deleting unimportant features permanently. [3](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/contents/regularization.html)

**Why the surviving values grow.** With dropout probability 0.25, a value 6 is kept with probability 0.75. If a retained value stayed 6, its expected training value would be 4.5. Inverted dropout instead outputs 8 when kept and zero when dropped, giving expectation $0.75\times8=6$. Evaluation can then be the identity operation without an extra scaling step.

**DropPath changes the unit being removed.** Elementwise dropout samples a mask for each activation. DropPath, often called stochastic depth in residual networks, drops an entire residual branch for an example. For a block $x+F(x)$, a dropped branch gives just x, preserving the skip path. The mask is broadcast across the branch's spatial/token/features dimensions rather than sampled separately for every coordinate.

These operations have different correlations: two features in the same DropPath branch disappear together, while elementwise dropout can retain one and remove another. Matching their keep probabilities does not make their regularization identical.

**Implementation checks.** Training mode should be stochastic; evaluation should be unchanged. Repeated draws should approximately preserve the expected activation when keep probability is positive. Explicitly handle p=0 and p=1 to avoid division by zero. A fixed seed is useful for tests, but reusing the exact same mask unintentionally on every training step reduces the intended variety of perturbations.

**Technical details and references.**

Inverted dropout multiplies retained values by 1/(1−p), preserving their expectation during training. DropPath samples one keep decision per batch example and broadcasts it over the residual branch; apply it before adding the skip connection. Evaluation is identity. p=1 is explicitly zero, avoiding division by zero. Element dropout and path dropout have different correlation structures despite sharing the scaling rule.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For keep probability $q$, inverted dropout is $\tilde x=mx/q$ with $m\sim Bernoulli(q)$, so $\mathbb E[\tilde x]=x$ when $q>0$. DropPath shares one mask across a whole example's residual branch. Matching expectations does not make the two operations equivalent: their noise covariance and regularization effects differ. [3](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/contents/regularization.html)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://d2l.ai/chapter_multilayer-perceptrons/dropout.html) and [2](https://docs.pytorch.org/vision/stable/generated/torchvision.ops.stochastic_depth.html).
